en: The Apadāna of the Elder Tikiṅkaṇipūjaka Ekapadumiya Chapter, Number 4 I am a bhikkhu who has attained the goal; I have lived the holy life. Having done what was to be done, I am freed from all fetters. In the past, when the Buddha Kassapa was the World-Honored One, I was a householder living in the city of Bandhumatī. At that time, I went to the monastery to see the Teacher, and there I saw the Buddha, the Great Sage, surrounded by his assembly. Then, with a joyful heart, I took three *kiṅkaṇi* flowers and offered them to the Blessed One, the Fully Enlightened One. Because of that root of merit, I have never fallen into the lower realms. For ninety-one eons, I have been a wheel-turning monarch. Now, having reached this final existence, I have become a monk. I have attained the destruction of the taints and dwell in peace. By offering those three *kiṅkaṇi* flowers to the Buddha, I have now realized the fruit of Arhatship. This is my own account of past deeds; it is the true history of my life. May you all rejoice in this, my declaration of the Dhamma. Thus ends the Apadāna of the Elder Tikiṅkaṇipūjaka.
"Not far from the Himālayas is a mountain named Bhūtagaṇa;
I had climbed up onto the top of a tree.
Having then plucked three kiṅkaṇī flowers, I—
Thirty-one eons ago, from this time,
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of three flowers.
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Tikiṅkaṇipūjaka speak these verses.
This is the fourth apadāna of the elder Tikiṅkaṇipūjaka.
